10.18632/oncotarget.15568.relation_note: Six EWSR1-NR4A3 cases; one initial RNA-quality failure. RET expression and two FOLR1 outliers are not validated drug-response biomarkers. Discussion reports pioglitazone exposure with 13 months stable disease but explicitly unknown drug contribution. Supplement and main-table treatment durations differ and require reconciliation.

10.3390/ijms19071855.relation_note: One somatic KIT p.D579del among 20 cases (five transcriptomes, 15 hotspot-only). Index patient responded to sunitinib but never received imatinib. This cannot explain all sunitinib responses or be merged with the later KIT p.W557G case. Figure 1 places the index EWSR1 junction upstream of the NR4A3 start codon; preserve transcript architecture in target comparisons.

free_links.evidence: Publisher Open archive abstract read 2026-09-12; contains 12 EMC and 7 myoepithelial tumours.

10.1016/j.labinv.2025.104344.relation_note: Caris summary has the matching Beyond NR4A3 title. Do not merge with the separate Suemitsu 2025 journal study on title similarity. Full poster and cohort overlap still require checking.

free_links.evidence: Open-access full text retrieved and read 2026-09-12; main PDF and two supplements recovered.

10.1136/bcr-2021-242039.relation_note: Single NR4A3-rearranged case with somatic KIT c.1669T>G (absent from blood). Three years stable disease on imatinib is reported; no serial response curve or functional assay of this variant in EMC is supplied. Do not generalize to every KIT variant or KIT-positive stain.

10.1186/2045-3329-2-22.relation_note: Two EWSR1-NR4A3 cases; one shows reported response, interruption-associated progression and response after restart. Figure 4 distinguishes infection from progression. Age, interruption duration and one dosing-unit entry differ across abstract/body/captions; precise exposure reconstruction needs reconciliation. Possible overlap with the 2014 sunitinib series remains unresolved.

10.1200/po.22.00039.relation_note: Single PGR-NR4A3 case with reported benefit on tamoxifen. Figure 1A additionally lists pelvic radiation at tamoxifen initiation and lung-nodule resection two months later; narrative does not fully describe these interventions. Their contribution needs reconciliation before attributing the prolonged outcome to tamoxifen alone. This is not evidence for unselected EMC.

10.1007/s13577-025-01250-7.relation_note: NCC-EMC1-C1 is distinct from USZ20-EMC1 and USZ22-EMC2. Public supplementary Tables 3 and 4 contain 221 screen rows and 24 IC50 rows; main text access remains unresolved.

10.1158/2767-9764.crc-26-0142.relation_note: Mixed-sarcoma screen includes HEMCSS/CVCL_1238. Model has an EWSR1-translocation caution; not counted as confirmed NR4A3-fusion evidence. Dataset is the same study, not an independent replication.

10.1186/s12885-016-2511-y.relation_note: Subanalysis of JapicCTI-121850: two EMC patients, both stable disease (PFS 13.0 and 7.4 months). The partial response and all three supportive-care controls were mesenchymal chondrosarcoma. Overlaps the 2015 parent trial and 2017/2020 pooled analyses.

10.1634/theoncologist.2016-0064.relation_note: Pooled JapicCTI-121850/121853 analysis. Table 1 contains two EMC patients, both from the original trabectedin arm; zero EMC patients in supportive care or crossover. These are not two additional EMC patients beyond the Morioka subanalysis.

10.1002/cam4.2991.relation_note: Reanalysis of the same Japanese trials: Table 1 again contains two EMC patients in the comparative trial and none in crossover. Figure 2 lists nine partial responders, all other histologies; its response-count difference from the 2017 report needs endpoint reconciliation.

10.1002/cncr.28728.relation_note: Related to NCT00642941 posted results, which separately report 11 EMC participants and zero complete/partial responses. Do not interpret pooled sarcoma responses as EMC responses; the main text stable-disease percentage has an ambiguous denominator.

10.1002/path.2445.relation_note: EMC protein and RNA observations plus rat-cell reporter experiments; does not establish a therapeutic dependency. Original figures and supplements remain under review.

10.1016/s1470-2045(19)30319-5.relation_note: Primary EMC pazopanib trial; separately published correction: DOI 10.1016/S1470-2045(19)30589-3 (PMID 31579002). Abstract read; full trial and correction text unresolved.

10.1002/path.5737.relation_note: Correction to Brenca 2019: the old data repository is unavailable; raw sequence reads moved to NCBI BioProject PRJNA692081. This notice does not add patients or efficacy results.

10.1002/path.5284.relation_note: Data-location correction DOI 10.1002/path.5737 replaces the defunct repository with NCBI BioProject PRJNA692081. Main article review remains incomplete.

10.1002/cncr.23978.relation_note: 32 evaluable treatment courses in 21 patients, with no objective responses. Table 4 includes imatinib stable disease >=6 months and interferon/sorafenib progression. Do not treat courses as independent patients or infer variant-specific response. Figure/layout review pending.

10.1186/2045-3329-3-16.relation_note: NR4A3-confirmed cohort: 11 treated, ten evaluable, four RECIST partial responses. Three patients censored at surgery. Retrospective selection and unresolved per-patient regimen descriptions prevent a causal comparison with older nonresponding series.

10.3389/fonc.2022.1042479.relation_note: Reports three EMC patients (two stable disease, one progression) from TrObs. Parent supplement labels only one EMC, with myxoid and extraskeletal mesenchymal chondrosarcoma as separate rows. The matching total does not prove which patients were reclassified. Resolve classification before pooling; this is not an independent cohort.

10.1007/s12032-017-1030-2.relation_note: Patient 7 is EMC: pazopanib alone, stable disease, time to progression eight months. Pazopanib/sirolimus patient 10 and both ramucirumab patients are conventional chondrosarcoma. Pooled survival is not an EMC estimate; molecular confirmation not reported.

10.3389/fonc.2020.00828.relation_note: 59-patient retrospective cohort, only 23 molecularly tested, all EWSR1-NR4A3. First-line anthracycline one PR among ten evaluable; all three second-line anthracycline recipients had PD. Treatment selection may confound the adverse chemotherapy/survival association. Eight selected drug holidays do not establish general safety. Three trabectedin cases may overlap other Italian reports; unresolved.

10.1186/s13018-025-06245-6.relation_note: Japanese registry: 171 included after excluding missing size/grade or <6 months follow-up. Six perioperative chemotherapy patients; indication bias, sparse events and wide intervals limit causal claims. Individual drug response and molecular confirmation are not supplied. Raw patient data are not public.

10.1159/000548238.relation_note: Single case with repeated local responses after surgery/SABR. The patient previously received six cycles of epirubicin/ifosfamide with reported partial response; the title does not mean no prior systemic treatment. Initial diagnosis was revised; molecular confirmation is not reported. Local control is not whole-body disease control or comparative survival evidence.

10.2147/cmar.s253201.relation_note: Three cases described as EMC. Main text/waterfall report one PR and two SD, but appendix codes two PR (patients 6, 14) and one SD (33). Molecular confirmation is not supplied. Response result unresolved; do not silently select a rate. Subtype HR 0.31 (95% CI 0.07–1.44), p=0.14, does not establish superior benefit. Substantial pooled toxicity is not an EMC-specific rate.

10.1186/s12885-018-4303-z.relation_note: Earlier Peking University mixed-sarcoma apatinib series reports three unspecified chondrosarcomas, all PR. No EMC subtype or patient crosswalk supplied; cannot add three EMC responders or establish overlap with2020EMCcases. All three2020EMCappendixrows have no prior systemic therapy, whereas2018text says untreated five were ASPS/epithelioid, which also prevents simple assumed matching. Three figures depict osteosarcoma, Ewing and soft-tissue groups, not individually identified EMC. No supplementary-material element; rawdata restricted.

10.1155/2019/3158590.relation_note: The sole EMC patient (52-year-old woman, Table 2, patient 10) received nanosomal docetaxel plus cyclophosphamide and had progressive disease. The pooled 50% response rate and 15.8-month survival are not EMC results. This is not an EMC gemcitabine/docetaxel response. Molecular confirmation, individual treatment line and response duration are not supplied. Retrospective manufacturer-funded study; no comparative evidence for formulation superiority or safety.

10.1186/s13569-020-00150-8.relation_note: Single localized shoulder recurrence after unplanned R1 excision: preoperative radiotherapy was followed by a specimen without viable tumor and wide re-excision; no relapse at 24 months. This is a reported pathological complete response, not proof that surgery can be omitted or survival improves. Molecular confirmation is not reported. The authors already propose testing vascular histology as a radiosensitivity correlate.

10.7759/cureus.432.relation_note: Single unresectable neck case: concurrent low-dose doxorubicin and radiotherapy produced a marked early response; follow-up was only one month after completion. Grade 3 mucositis and dermatitis occurred. Carboplatin/paclitaxel was planned from TLE3/PGP/TUBB3/ERCC1 IHC, not reported as administered or effective. No NR4A3 confirmation reported. Cannot separate chemotherapy from radiation benefit or establish durable control.

10.4172/clinical-practice.1000433.relation_note: Single metastatic case with repeated local radiation responses during third-line trabectedin, after pazopanib and doxorubicin progression. New lesions and mediastinal progression occurred between radiation courses. No comparator separates radiation-alone effects from synergy; the authors proposed the combination before this review. Molecular confirmation and the pazopanib trial identifier are not supplied. Do not count this as an independent pazopanib cohort or continuous whole-body progression-free survival.

free_links.evidence: All nine pages and six embedded figures retrieved/read2026-09-12; hashed retrieval receipt retained.

10.5114/jcb.2022.115161.relation_note: One NR4A3-rearranged case treated at three metastatic sites with brachytherapy. Reported local control was 41 months for inguinal disease and 36 months for breast/popliteal lesions; lung metastases were not treated or quantified as a response endpoint. One grade 2 dermatitis event and no reported late toxicity do not establish comparative safety or superiority over external radiation. The narrative incorrectly gives D90 as a percentage; Table 1 gives Gy. Supplement two-page PDF text and all five embedded images accounting for four figures read.

10.1155/2020/2684746.relation_note: Three selected patients without systemic treatment followed for 50, 70 and 126 months. Case 3 underwent palliative amputation, later had breathlessness and an EMC-positive pathological hip fracture, and died from colon cancer complications. Thus not all follow-up was event-free or asymptomatic despite abstract/discussion wording. EWSR1 rearrangement is reported; NR4A3-specific testing and lung biopsy are not. Patient-perspective immune-control statement has no accompanying immune assay. This is natural-history context, not evidence that observation is generally safe or equivalent to treatment. No tables or supplements in indexed XML.

10.1093/jscr/rjaa503.relation_note: Single pelvic/gluteal case treated by resection, argon-laser electrofulguration and peritoneal lavage. Uneventful postoperative course reported, but no long-term recurrence or survival outcome or NR4A3 confirmation. Does not establish benefit from the adjuncts. A phase-II study is proposed without a reported trial identifier or results. Intraoperative treatment here is not intraoperative radiotherapy. No tables or supplements in indexed XML.

10.55730/1300-0144.5422.relation_note: Thirteen-patient retrospective surgical series; all five chemotherapy recipients had metastatic disease. Worse survival in that group does not establish chemotherapy harm or ineffectiveness. Drug names and response endpoints are not supplied. Tumor-size cut-off was selected in the same small dataset, without external validation. Table1 follow-up range14–86 months differs from24–96 in body/Table2; age maximum75 differs from73 in abstract/body. Figure1 caption describes hyaline cartilage with small undifferentiated cells; NR4A3 confirmation is absent. Diagnostic classification requires expert reconciliation, not an automated re-diagnosis. All body, abstract, references, three tables and four figures read; no supplement element.

10.1007/s00432-025-06316-5.relation_note: Narrative review, not a new treatment cohort. Complete body, references, four table texts, four main figures and graphical abstract read; no supplement element. Radiation section duplicates the same long external-radiation narrative under Qiu2014 and Takagawa2022; the primary Takagawa report is instead the87-year-old ankle/three-site brachytherapy case. Do not count the repeated narrative as another patient. Prognosis section and Table1 give different post-metastasis survival figures, and the conclusion alternates pazopanib as initial versus post-anthracycline therapy. These statements require primary-source reconciliation. Some anatomical examples cite mesenchymal chondrosarcoma rather than myxoid; inclusion cannot rely on this review alone. Its references are discovery pointers, not completed primary reading or validated treatment recommendations.
